questions.question: Are the five observed destination listings the five products the requester intended?
questions.what_we_know: The five dated shop records keep each submitted link and its observed redirect target separate; all five intended-ASIN fields are blank.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The requester’s intended ASIN and official listing URL for each of the five links. All five intended fields are blank.
questions.why_it_matters: A correct redirect observation does not prove the product is the one requested; every recommendation, guide and product CTA depends on intended identity.
questions.how_to_discover: Ask the requester to confirm the intended ASIN and official listing for each of the five links; record the confirmation date/source separately from the observed redirect. Do not call the submitted short links invalid.

questions.question: Which marketplace and audience should the publication serve?
questions.what_we_know: The five observed destinations are Amazon.com listings. This does not establish the target country, reader location, currency or Associates marketplace.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The intended audience geography, supported marketplace(s), language and whether the site should remain US-only.
questions.why_it_matters: Product availability, links, terms and commission schedules depend on the selected marketplace; the requester’s physical location is not evidence of target audience.
questions.how_to_discover: Confirm the intended audience and the country/account association in Associates Central; read the current Operating Agreement schedule for each planned locale before adding localized links.

questions.question: Is the Associates account enrolled and eligible for the intended product data/API workflow?
questions.what_we_know: The repository cites official Associates/Creators API prerequisites and policies; the public build deliberately leaves price, review and availability fields out unless an approved source is available.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Account standing, API access, current eligibility and permission for any requested analytical use.
questions.why_it_matters: It gates dynamic product data and any use of Program Content in automated research or content generation.
questions.how_to_discover: Check account status and current API documentation in the account; before using Program Content in analysis or AI workflows, verify applicable policy and required written approval from the official terms.

questions.question: Who is the named human editor, and what publishing cadence can they sustain?
questions.what_we_know: Question-shaped guides, a feed and sitemap build path exist. No named human reviewer is recorded. A 14-day cadence has appeared as a proposal, not an owner-approved schedule.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The reviewer’s real name, authority, review time and adopted cadence.
questions.why_it_matters: Authorship and human review cannot be generated by code; without a real reviewer, a byline or “tested” language would mislead.
questions.how_to_discover: Name an actual editor and set a sustainable interval; do not publish a human byline, first-person test or experience claim until the person and evidence exist.

questions.question: Have the products been used or tested first-hand?
questions.what_we_know: The current product records are listing observations; the repository contains no first-hand testing record. FTC guidance distinguishes genuine experience from claims about an untried product.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Whether anyone will obtain and test the five products, or what the method and evidence would be.
questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether reviews can describe actual use or must remain clearly limited to listing-based buyer questions.
questions.how_to_discover: Decide whether to test; if yes, record the reviewer, unit, dates, setup, protocol and observations. If not, keep the copy to sourced listing facts and explicit limits.

questions.question: Which publisher name, voice and visual identity should be canonical?
questions.what_we_know: Current pages use several working identities, including Zone3, Zone3 Kitchen, Air Fryer Field Notes and The Crisp Report. A final brand choice is not recorded.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The chosen publisher name, palette, voice, trademark/domain clearance and whether the name should span both product categories.
questions.why_it_matters: Multiple names and voices make the site look assembled from parallel builds instead of edited as one publication.
questions.how_to_discover: Choose one name and voice; check name/domain/handle availability through the relevant official registries before adopting it. Until then, treat existing names as working labels.

questions.question: What analytics/reporting stack and privacy boundary should be used?
questions.what_we_know: The campaign ledger is empty. The repository has a five-event prototype proposal, but enabled=false and endpoint_url is empty; a collector script is present but is not hosted. GitHub Pages is static and its documentation states visitor IP addresses are logged.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Owner approval of the event proposal, an actual host/runtime, application and provider/network logging, IP handling, retention, access controls, applicable notice/consent requirements, and authorized conversion reports.
questions.why_it_matters: No endpoint is live. “Privacy-preserving” cannot be claimed until the actual collection path and host logging are verified.
questions.how_to_discover: Keep counting OFF. Review the existing proposed definitions; select a runtime only if needed; read official host documentation and inspect real network/access logs, IP handling and retention in staging before activation. Use authorized Associates reports for conversion/order figures.

questions.question: What measured reader queries or topic signals exist?
questions.what_we_know: The repository contains question-led working titles, a feed and sitemap, but no dated Search Console query export or measured reader-query dataset.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Which queries have impressions/clicks, their dates, the canonical property’s baseline and whether readers reach the product guides.
questions.why_it_matters: Without measured queries, “trending” and “high-converting” would be guesses; the next topic cannot be selected from evidence yet.
questions.how_to_discover: After choosing the canonical URL, verify the site property in Search Console and save a dated query export; compare equivalent date windows, and keep topic ideas labelled as hypotheses until data exists.

questions.question: Does the disclosure placement need a formal counsel review?
questions.what_we_know: The exact Associates disclosure is on the publication pages; the Operating Agreement and FTC sources in the register describe clear/prominent placement and disclosure with the endorsement.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Whether the owner wants a formal legal review or has additional jurisdiction-specific requirements.
questions.why_it_matters: Disclosure must remain visible alongside recommendations across every template and category page.
questions.how_to_discover: Have counsel review the shared page templates and any new endpoint/cookie/analytics notices before deployment; keep the existing disclosure in place regardless.

questions.question: Should the two meat-thermometer listings be part of the same publication as the three air-fryer listings?

questions.question: Which reader-facing page set is canonical, and what happens to duplicated layers?
questions.what_we_know: The repository contains the root publication, /shop/, /guides/, /site/, /read/, /marketing/ and /articles/ reader-facing areas, alongside audit pages. Several overlap in product and guide coverage.
questions.what_we_dont_know: The owner’s accepted canonical page set, final brand, and whether non-canonical pages should be merged, archived, redirected or kept as distinct content.
questions.why_it_matters: Duplicated content splits internal navigation and makes the publication feel generated. The prompt’s “one site to index” needs a concrete page inventory, not a second microsite.
questions.how_to_discover: Recommended default: root publication plus /shop/ categories and /guides/ articles on one host. Map unique content and every inbound link before any archive/redirect/noindex change; record the chosen set in the review console.

questions.question: Which five analytics events should be collected, and where can the endpoint run?
questions.what_we_know: The brief asks for five event definitions but does not name them. The repository contains five proposed definitions in data/shop/measurement.json, generated config disabled with an empty endpoint URL, and an unhosted collector prototype; no event collection is recorded.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Owner approval or revision of the proposal; deployment/runtime choice; actual host logs, IP handling, retention and access controls; applicable notice/consent review; and authorized report import.
questions.why_it_matters: A browser event is not an Amazon conversion. Any custom click counter must leave the Amazon link direct and must not create a redirect or imply user-level attribution.
questions.how_to_discover: Review the five existing proposed names and fields as a draft, not as live tracking. Keep the feature OFF; inspect host documentation and real staging logs/retention, then obtain owner and privacy review before activation. No Amazon checkout event is available to the browser.

questions.question: Which photography source and rights allow product images to appear?
questions.what_we_know: The Operating Agreement treats images as Program Content; the five-product register has no image-rights/provenance record. No rights confirmation is inferred.
questions.what_we_dont_know: Whether an approved Associates feed or written permission exists, and who owns any original photography on the site.
questions.why_it_matters: The design should not show generated, scraped or copied product photography as if it were genuine product imagery.
questions.how_to_discover: Use a permitted Amazon-served image source or original owner-created photography with documented rights; otherwise stay text-first and use original non-photographic diagrams.

Review the existing five-event schema as a proposal. The counter config is OFF and the collector is unhosted; verify a selected host's real access/network logs, IP handling, retention and controls before any activation. Use authorized Associates reports for conversions.
Verify the canonical property and obtain dated query data before describing topics as popular or using search performance as a cadence signal.
Publish only approved, human-reviewed buyer-question guides with official source links, required disclosure, rel="sponsored" outbound links and feed/sitemap updates.
Rebuild and run the full release gates after each generator change; leave unconfirmed values blank and flagged.

paths.name: Shopfront first, lab underneath
paths.thesis: A buyer decides in seconds at the shelf; the verification machinery stays one click away but never above the fold. The site stops reading like an audit by changing what is FIRST, not by adding decoration.
steps: Open site/index.html with the three-question chooser already built for this purpose (decision D-23 in the brief's list) — move it above the product cards; every answer deep-links to the comparison row it affects.

Give each product card a 'fits you if / not for you if' pair of lines generated ONLY from quoted listing features — the generator already blocks any other sentence (i2_gate G6/G7), so catchiness comes from layout, not from invented claims.
Below the cards, one strip: 'New this week from the guides desk' fed by the same register that now backs feed.xml; dated, never ranked.
Disclosure strip stays exactly where it is (above the fold, every page, repeated in the footer) — the polish must not move it, and the lint enforces that it wasn't.
Keep every dashboard surface (flagged, sources, verification, decision pages) reachable from the footer and the single nav group — already true; do not add nav items, fold new ones in.
paths.resolves: The look half of SUG-01 and SUG-04; the brief's 'lead with the products' rule; consistent with S-17/S-19 as implemented.
paths.effort: One generator pass over site/ home + front-door region; no new data files; every gate already exists.
paths.risk: Low. Worst case the page reverts on a rebuild — the same self-healing pattern the feed uses now covers it.
paths.do_not: No prices, no star ratings, no review counts, no 'bestseller' badge until the API feed exists (2(b)/6(t)); no 'trending' without a dated first-party snapshot (the evidence rule already adopted).

paths.name: Magazine desk: voice and cadence carry it
paths.thesis: The fastest way to stop reading like AI slop is a real editorial calendar with a named human gate: one dated question per week, an author byline, and a 'what changed since last read' box that only a desk that re-reads sources can write.
steps: Adopt the cadence in the review below: one guide per week, each new guide lands in sitemap + feed automatically because both are register-driven now.

Add a byline block ('Field Notes desk — reviewed by: <name>') once Q5 names the human reviewer; until then the reviewed_by line stating 'no human editor' stays (it is already there; polishing would mean removing it, which we will not do).
Two held topics become publishable ONLY with owner inputs: testing/first-hand use (Q6) or the API for figures (Q4); do not write them softer to ship them.
Keep titles question-shaped like the five live guides; the brief's own suggested titles are all published — the next topic should come from the D8 query report, not from instinct.
paths.resolves: SUG-02, SUG-03, SUG-10, S-07's cadence half, and the 'catchy trendy articles' ask — honestly: catchy within what the compliance gates allow.
paths.effort: Editorial continuity, not code: the machinery (register, lint, feed, sitemap) already carries a weekly page in under an hour.
paths.risk: Cadence decays without a named owner; the site must never ship a 'latest' widget that goes stale — the register dates everything for exactly this reason.
paths.do_not: No synthetic social proof, no 'most popular', no AI-author persona names.

paths.name: Consolidate, then decorate
paths.thesis: Three parallel reader layers (site/, read/, marketing/) say near-the-same things about the same three products in three voices. That is both the strongest 'generated' tell and the reason search cannot pick a winner. One canonical layer fixes the findability ask and most of the slop feel at once.
steps: Owner answers Q12 (choose the canonical layer). Recommendation recorded here: promote site/ (the layer with the working house lint and release gates) and mark read/ + marketing/ as companion research with cross-links, not duplicates.
One navigation, one feed (the new feed.xml grows to cover the layer chosen), one sitemap (already covers everything; consolidation is a link-and-banner change, not a build change).
Fold the surviving extras (photography once S-18 decides, any API data once Q4 clears) into the chosen layer only, so polish is not written three times.
paths.resolves: 'One site to index and a reason to rank it' from the brief; Z14-F-04; the duplication note; most of Q7's brand-open residue.
paths.effort: Small edits, but touches the most shared files in the repo — must be ONE integration session (per the coordination protocol), not three parallel ones.
paths.risk: Link churn: internal cross-links and the sitemap shift. The gates in scripts/ catch every broken one before push.
paths.do_not: Do not delete the losing layers (history rule: archives stay); do not hand-merge the three feeds of copy into one without re-running every gate on the result.

review_2026_11_17_ed27e766.note: This review follows the five-product/two-category intake. It separates observed destinations from owner intent, notes the requester-supplied tracking ID as unverified, and treats the existing five-event counter/collector as a disabled, unhosted prototype—not live analytics.

recommended_path.name: One publication, categories as sections, evidence one click away
recommended_path.summary: Use the existing root publication as the public front door, /shop/ for category/product destinations, and /guides/ for buyer questions. Keep one brand and one grouped “Research & governance” navigation group plus the footer. Move unique material out of overlapping /site/, /read/, /marketing/ and /articles/ layers before any archive/redirect/noindex change.
recommended_path.why: This matches the already-shipped root publication and the explicit “one site to index” request while avoiding another competing microsite.
recommended_path.status: Recommended proposal; not yet applied to duplicate routes.

paths.name: Shopfront polish first
paths.thesis: Keep the existing root publication and make the next design pass buyer-led, not process-led.
steps: Lead with the two category choices, then show the five observed listing cards with clear status; do not imply intent or superiority.
Keep the four question-led guides visible as editorial choices, and distinguish working hypotheses from measured queries.
Group audit, decisions, sources and flagged records under one “Research & governance” menu item and repeat the group in the footer.
Do not move or soften the disclosure strip; keep it under the masthead on every page and repeat it in the footer.
paths.resolves: The product-first front page, grouped navigation and disclosure requirements.
paths.effort: Small-to-medium; mostly template and layout edits, no new product data.
paths.risk: Low if the current generator/publish passes remain authoritative.
paths.do_not: Do not add price/rating/review badges, untested verdicts, “trending” claims or generated product photography.

paths.name: Magazine desk and measured cadence
paths.thesis: Make the site feel published through a real editor, a review gate and a steady question-led calendar—not through filler.
steps: Use one question per guide and cite every factual answer to an official source.
Adopt one guide every 14 days only after a human reviewer is named; this interval is a proposed setting, not an owner decision.
After Search Console is connected, choose the next question from dated query reports; until then use the supplied titles as hypotheses, not popularity claims.
Add each accepted guide through the existing register-driven feed/sitemap build.
Use a named byline only when the named person has actually reviewed the article; never create a fictional desk author.
paths.resolves: Authorship, cadence, question-shaped topics, organic measurement and the anti-slop request.
paths.effort: Ongoing editorial operations; the feed/sitemap parts are already automated.
paths.risk: Medium if the human gate is skipped or dates are left stale.
paths.do_not: Do not use “trending”, “best”, “we tested” or seasonal urgency without appropriate dated evidence.

paths.name: Consolidate the reader architecture before more content
paths.thesis: One public publication with clear categories; no parallel brand or near-duplicate page set.
steps: Treat root /Zone3/ as the recommended front door; retain /shop/ category pages and /guides/ as distinct same-site destinations.
Inventory every unique claim and internal link in /site/, /read/, /marketing/ and /articles/ before deciding whether to merge, archive or redirect.
Keep audit, sources, decisions and flagged items reachable from one grouped nav and the footer, not in the buyer hero.
After a route map is approved, rebuild sitemap/feed and crawl all internal links; do not apply noindex/redirect rules speculatively.
paths.resolves: The “one site to index” request, category clarity and duplicated-brand problem.
paths.effort: Largest path; needs a single integration pass and a before/after link inventory.
paths.risk: Medium because route changes can strand links or discard unique evidence.
paths.do_not: Do not delete, redirect or noindex an existing page until its unique content and inbound links are mapped.

analytics.status: Proposal only — the repository prototype is disabled and no collection endpoint is hosted.
analytics.note: These are the five event definitions already recorded as PROPOSED in data/shop/measurement.json; the owner brief does not name or approve them. The browser counter is configured OFF and endpoint_url is empty. No live site events or conversion data are recorded. The collector script is not a deployed service.

events.name: page_view
events.fields: event name, page path (no query string or hash), UTC day, protocol version.
events.purpose: The existing draft counts page loads by path/day only; not unique visitors or sessions.

events.name: outbound_click
events.when: A click on a link marked rel="sponsored" to Amazon.
events.fields: event name, page path, link host, and only a 4–20 character alphanumeric last path segment when present.
events.purpose: Proposed outbound click count; no query string, tag value, full URL, person identifier or Amazon conversion.

events.name: guide_view
events.when: A non-index guide page under /guides/ or /site/guides/ loads.
events.fields: event name, page path, UTC day.
events.purpose: Proposed guide-page count; no visitor identity.

events.name: intent_view
events.fields: event name, page path, UTC day.
events.purpose: Proposed count for the intent-record page; no individual visitor profile.

events.name: flag_view
events.when: The flagged-for-review page or publication-pass page loads.
events.fields: event name, page path, UTC day.
events.purpose: Proposed count for governance pages; no individual visitor profile.

privacy_rules: The checked-in browser rules write no cookies or browser storage and generate/send no visitor identifier.
The prototype suppresses sends when globalPrivacyControl is true or Do Not Track is 1; with enabled=false or an empty endpoint URL, it sends nothing.
The proposed payload omits user agent, referrer and query strings; do not call raw page views sessions or clicks conversions.
Keep sponsored Amazon anchors direct; do not add a redirect or change the href to measure a click.

Do not activate any runtime until its official logging/retention documentation and actual network/access logs, IP handling, retention, access controls and applicable notice/consent requirements have been reviewed.
Use authorized Associates first-party reports for order/conversion figures; do not create a browser checkout event or forecast.
analytics.deployment_gate: GitHub Pages is static and its official documentation states visitor IP addresses are logged. The repository has a local collector prototype, but no runtime is selected or hosted, its config is OFF with endpoint_url empty, and no host's real logging/retention behavior is verified. This is not live analytics or a present-tense privacy claim.

cadence.proposal: One human-reviewed, question-shaped guide every 14 days after an editor is named; every accepted guide is registered and rebuilt into sitemap and RSS feed.
cadence.topic_rule: Use Search Console query data after the canonical property is verified. Until a dated query report exists, use the requested titles and seasonal ideas as editorial hypotheses, never as trending/popularity claims.
seasonal_hypotheses: A pre-holiday kitchen-appliance checklist: what can a listing tell you, and what can’t it?
Before grilling season: which digital and wireless thermometer details should a buyer compare?
A small-kitchen reset: what capacity and counter-space questions should you ask before choosing an air fryer?
cadence.note: Cadence and seasonal framing are proposals, not measured demand. Add seasonal expiry/review dates and source checks before publication.

how_to_choose: Use DP-C as the recommended default because the brief asks for one site to index; record Accept/Reject/Defer against SUG-11 in the review console before route changes.
DP-A can be accepted with DP-C as a visual refinement. DP-B is an editorial operating rule and can run alongside either after a real editor is named.

For SUG-12, use the five definitions in the repository as a review draft only. Keep collection OFF; host/runtime and actual logging/retention/privacy review are prerequisites, not a consequence of accepting the schema.
For product identity and Special Links, use the account workflow rather than accepting observed redirects as intent or compliance evidence.
Nothing on this page makes a route, analytics or account change by itself. Keep unresolved items visibly flagged.
